topic: How does Face ID actually recognize you

beats.narration: Your iPhone unlocks just by looking at it. But what actually happens in that split second between your glance and the lock screen disappearing?
It starts with the TrueDepth camera system. The moment you raise your phone, an infrared flood illuminator lights up your face with invisible I-R light, even in complete darkness.
Then a dot projector fires over thirty thousand invisible I-R dots onto your face. An infrared camera reads the pattern. Flat photos can't replicate this because the dots encode actual three-D depth.
The depth map goes straight to a dedicated neural engine on the A-series chip. It converts the raw dot cloud into a compact mathematical model of your face, not an image, just numbers.
That math model is sent to the Secure Enclave, a hardened coprocessor isolated from the rest of the system. Your enrolled face data never leaves this chip. Not even Apple can extract it.

The Secure Enclave compares the new model against your stored enrollment. It tolerates natural changes, glasses, beard growth, aging, because it continuously updates its reference model with each successful unlock.
The whole pipeline, I-R flood, dot projection, neural network, Secure Enclave comparison, runs in under four hundred milliseconds. That is Face ID.
